> == Vendored crates are byte-identical to crates.io (independent of tools/vendor-check) ==
> For all six crates, not just smoltcp and heapless:
> - downloaded the .crate from static.crates.io;
> - compared its SHA-256 with the cksum in the live crates.io sparse index (index.crates.io);
> - unpacked it and ran `diff -r` against vendor/<name> at 737a0a41a.
> Result: smoltcp b6f8b28a.., heapless 25ba4bd8.., managed 0ca88d72.., hash32 47d60b12.., stable_deref_trait 6ce2be8d.., byteorder 1fd0f258..: index = download = README, and every tree is IDENTICAL (no added, removed or changed files; the crates' own Cargo.lock files included).
> 
> == The build really uses the vendored copies ==
> `cargo tree -p redoubt-vendor-check -e normal,build --target riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf` resolves smoltcp, byteorder, heapless, hash32, stable_deref_trait and managed to /tmp/d3cr1/vendor/*, and cfg-if 1.0.0 and bitflags 1.3.2 to the registry. defmt is in no build graph. The release builds for riscv64imac and riscv32imac pass offline. `cargo test -p redoubt-vendor-check`: 3 passed. The Cargo.lock diff is additions only: no existing package's lock entry moved.
> 
> == Deviations: sound ==
> - **Kept out of members, patch paths used.** Right: members would pull their dev-dependencies into the lockfile and build std features under `cargo test --workspace`. The plan file still says 'workspace member (getrandom precedent)'; bring decision 1 into line with what was done.
> - **cfg-if and bitflags left to Cargo.lock.** Sound: both are macro-only and already locked for the kernel and test programs, and the test pins version and checksum.
> - **defmt and thiserror 2.0.0 locked but unbuilt.** Confirmed: they are absent from every graph, and a proc-macro runs only when compiled. `cargo fetch` or a non-offline `cargo metadata` would download them, which is harmless.
> - **Excluded from the unsafe ratchet: acceptable.** vendor-check pins every byte by SHA-256, so any change to heapless fails a test, which is stronger than a count ratchet, and the code isn't ours to reduce. Conditions:
>   - the promised reading of heapless Vec and LinearMap lands with or before ipd's stack commit, listing their unsafe blocks;
>   - optionally, vendor-check records the unsafe count in the heapless files smoltcp actually compiles, so an upgrade diff shows the delta.
>   The rustfmt exclusion is fine.
> 
> P2. vendor-check proves integrity since vendoring, not provenance. SHA256SUMS is generated from the tree itself (README 'Updating'), and the VENDORED .crate checksums are compared only against the README, never against the bytes. So someone could edit a file, regenerate the sums and pass. Say that in the README and the test doc. Add the provenance recipe (download the .crate, compare with the index cksum, unpack, diff -r), or an opt-in networked mode, and require it in the review of any vendor update. For 737a0a41a I have done it (above).
> 
> P3 notes:
> - The lock test doesn't check that the patch paths point at vendor/<name>: a path package shows no source wherever it lives. A `cargo metadata` manifest_path assertion would close that.
> - Path dependencies aren't lint-capped, so heapless prints lifetime-elision warnings in every build. That's harmless, since nothing builds with -D warnings, but it will be noisy.
> 
> == Kind generator: existing generated files byte-identical ==
> At ae5bb4af5, `cargo run -p redoubt-wire-gen -- --check` exits 0 with tables unchanged from the parent, so the new generator reproduces every committed file byte for byte. Generator tests: 17 passed. The parse is strict:
> - a send's reply must be '-';
> - an unknown kind, a short row, or a Kind header without a marker is refused;
> - is_send() is emitted only when a table has a send.
> At 737a0a41a the check is still clean, and redoubt-wire's tests pass.
> P3: a send still gets a generated FrameReply and a REPLIES layout (Reply::Frame). That's harmless, but a receiver could encode a reply for a send; consider emitting no reply type or layout for sends.
> 
> == force-legacy: additive ==
> b3306141f adds `-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false` only when boot.disk or boot.net is set. `virtio_devices` is the only device-argument path (main.rs:331). A case with neither gets no arguments, and a unit test asserts it. The only affected cases are bench-ssh-guest and bench-virtio-devices. virtio-probe reads magic, device ID and the MAC at 0x100, which are the same in both layouts. Testbench unit tests: 11 passed, including restrict=on for every network. Nit: the tests' temp disk name is per pid, so tests running in parallel share it (harmless).
